workflow-e3620ce7-3a81-4ca1-ab25-599de2a.goal: Add a provider-agnostic, privacy-safe product usage and entitlement foundation for LeadFinder. Model bounded capabilities and search-usage events without assuming prices, plans or customer facts. Support deterministic validation and aggregation for searches used, successful searches, degraded searches and remaining quota only when an explicit limit is supplied. Never store raw lead contact data, access codes, cookies, tokens or free-form notes. Include tests for invalid limits, replay-safe event IDs, aggregation and privacy. Keep this as an adapter-ready domain layer; do not wire billing, external APIs, production deployment or user communications.

workflow-e1a21e3d-75a5-4546-b39a-7c7efac.goal: Continue LeadFinder productization from the latest integrated work without duplicating PRs #12 or #13. Focus on the next safe foundation for real multi-user use: provider-agnostic durable per-subject persistence contracts and a server-side product request context that can bind authenticated opaque subject, capabilities, workspace ownership and future usage accounting. Read integration/product-v1 and feature/access-entitlements-v1 first. Prefer deterministic contracts and tests over choosing a database vendor. Do not invent prices, plans, customer facts or quotas. Do not add billing, payment providers, production secrets, external user communications, production deployment or merges. Do not implement process-memory or browser-only counters as durable quota enforcement. Keep private/customer data out of logs and fixtures. Produce a reviewable branch/PR only after full tests, lint and build pass.

inspectionEvidence.summary: Inspected supplied discovery and relevance code. Recommend one bounded improvement: recognize plural Spanish barber queries through the existing hairdresser strategy. No files changed or tests executed in this read-only analysis.
findings: src/providers/niche-mapper.ts recognizes barbería and barberia as Peluquerías aliases but omits barberías and barberias; getNicheDiscoveryStrategy requires an exact normalized alias match, so Barberías returns null.

src/providers/niche-relevance.ts falls back to literal niche matching for unknown queries. Consequently, Barberías with evidence name Barbería López and taxonomy hairdresser scores 0, whereas the recognized singular query uses the hairdresser strategy.

src/providers/osm-business-search.ts gives unknown niches empty canonical filters and invokes the initial Overpass query without a text term. For Barberías this produces empty-regex selectors before subsequent literal text expansion, potentially spending discovery budget on unrelated entities.

The single recommended change is adding barberías and barberias to the existing Peluquerías aliases. Add regression assertions in src/providers/osm-logic.test.ts for singular/plural strategy equivalence and in src/providers/niche-relevance.test.ts for Barberías matching Barbería López and hairdresser taxonomy while rejecting restaurante evidence. The supplied tests currently contain no barber-query regression cases.

inspectionEvidence.summary: Inspected supplied repository contents and identified one bounded improvement: recognize plural barber-shop searches through the existing hairdressing discovery strategy. No files changed or tests executed.
findings: src/providers/niche-mapper.ts recognizes singular 'barbería' and 'barberia' under Peluquerías but omits 'barberías' and 'barberias'; getNicheDiscoveryStrategy requires an exact normalized alias match, so 'Barberías' returns null.

src/providers/niche-relevance.ts consequently uses its unknown-niche fallback for 'Barberías'. Evidence such as name 'Barbería López' and taxonomy 'hairdresser' scores 0 because neither contains the whole normalized plural term 'barberias'.

src/providers/osm-business-search.ts uses a fallback strategy without canonical filters for this query instead of the existing Peluquerías filters, and discards relevance scores below 45. This creates a concrete recall gap for a current commercial focus.

Recommend exactly one improvement: add the plural Spanish barber-shop aliases to the existing strategy. Add regression assertions in src/providers/osm-logic.test.ts for accented and unaccented plural strategy resolution, and in src/providers/niche-relevance.test.ts for singular-name and hairdresser-taxonomy evidence queried as 'Barberías'. The supplied tests do not cover these cases.
